0x008ACEE0.name: StewardObject
0x008ACEE0.note: The race Steward. docs/26 mislabels this 'ForceFeedbackBase'. Holds the TRACK-SECTOR FLAG TABLE that HUDFlagRendererMain's yellow branch reads: +0x108 float scale (distance*scale = segment index), +0x10C int segment count (29 on this track), +0x110 ptr to {int32 state; float end_distance} stride 8, +0x114 ptr to the game's own previous-state int32 copy used for change detection. state 0 = green, 2 = YELLOW (live-verified with a yellow flag flying: segment 4 held 2, all others 0). The state field is 6 bits — events are encoded as state | (segment << 6) and decoded by ParseMidiBitstream_004d1a50 as w>>6 / w&0x3F. WRITER: sub_4D1730, every frame, clears the whole table then re-marks the segment of any non-DNF car whose forward velocity is under a threshold, so a yellow means 'slow car here' and NOTHING written into this table survives a frame. See investigations/yellow_flag/README.md.

0x1065.name: ParkingBrakeIndicator

0x3D70.name: EngineLifeRemaining
sources: live:investigations/engine_lifetime 2026-07-25 (armed on an AI, in-game confirmed)
0x3D70.note: COMPONENT LIFE COUNTDOWN, seconds remaining. FuelConsumptionAndWear_004ed960 decrements four of these by delta-time each tick (`this[i+3929] -= a2` for i=0..3, gated on sub_4D21D0) and when one goes negative writes the matching ReasonCode into veh+0x4068 and fails that component. NOTE the decompiled `this` is veh+0xC, NOT the vehicle base, so index 3929 resolves to veh+0x3D70. Live: healthy cars read 20000-41000 s; a car whose engine had just blown read -1.0 in the engine slot. POKE-PROVEN 2026-07-25: writing 0.5 to the engine slot on a healthy running AI (Sarrazin) fired ReasonCode=1 within 0.2 s, the engine wound down 1577->0 rpm, and 5 s later the GAME ITSELF set FinishState=2 + RetiredFlag=1. Arming this trigger produces a genuine failure; no state is forged. Distinct from OilTemp (0x3D10), which is only a readout -- pinning it at 200 C for 24 s did nothing. This slot fires ReasonCode 1 Engine. AI-ONLY: the decrement is gated on veh+0x32C8==1, which is 0 for the human driver (see 0x32C8). FULL-RACE MEASUREMENT 2026-07-25: drains at exactly 1.000/s for all 21 simulated cars over 65 minutes, unaffected by oil temp (101->113 C) or revs, and keeps draining on a car that has already retired. It is a plain wall clock. Lowest value reached in a 53-lap race was 10400 s, so AI components can never fail from this counter within a race distance -- scripted failures via the veh+0x4144 table are the only path.

0x44C0.name: QualifyingAbilityNorm
0x44C0.note: LIVE VALUE-MATCHED 2026-07-27, 21/21 cars: = (22 - rcd QualifyingAbility)/22 (fit slope -0.045455 = -1/22, intercept 1.0). The qualifying twin of RaceAbilityNorm (0x44C4) but WITHOUT the quadratic AI-difficulty-slider damping: 0x44C4 carries a x(slider/100)^2 factor (0.8464 at slider 92) and this one does not. Lower raw ability = higher norm = faster.

0x44C4.name: RaceAbilityNorm
0x44C4.note: LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-26: (22 - RaceAbility)/22 x (AIDifficultySlider/100)^2, verified on 8 drivers (RA 1.8..10.6) at slider 92 with residual < 0.001 -- quadratic slider damping exact at 0.8464. CLAMPS AT 1.0: Alonso (effective RA ~ -82 in memory) reads exactly 1.0 while his unclamped 0x44F4 runs to 1.7504. Lower raw RA = higher norm = faster. Baked once at session init; feed for the per-frame pace walk at 0x453C. NOTE: effective RA can differ from the loose SeasonData rcd when a randomizer/save pipeline is active (Webber ~7.30 vs file 11.3) -- both formulas still hold with the effective value.  CORROBORATED 2026-07-27 by an independent method (live affine value-match vs the shipped .rcd files, tools/match_values.py): 21/21 cars fit 0.8464 - 0.038473 x RaceAbility, which is algebraically identical to 0.8464 x (22 - RaceAbility)/22 and recovers the (92/100)^2 = 0.8464 slider term without being told it. No clamping and no randomizer divergence in this session.

Same /100 x scalar shape as AbilityBaselineScalar (0x44F4) but NOT inverted - 0x44F4 uses (1 - RA/100), this uses RainAbility/100 directly, so here a HIGHER raw value gives a higher field.

0x44F8.name: TrackAggressionEffective
0x44F8.note: LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-26: = AIRealism(0x7D017C) x rcd TrackAggression (default 1.0 when the rcd key is absent), clamped >= 0.01. Schumacher and De La Rosa (no rcd key) both read exactly 0.6878 = the player's PLR AI Realism. Consumed every frame by AISteering: desired follow gap x(2-a) floored at 20-10a m; side-by-side window 4-a; per-opponent pressure accumulator += a x max(1,closing) while gap < (1+a) x 20 m, -5 beyond, cap 450 (250 under one flag). This is the PLR 'AI Realism' knob's only effect. NOT recomputed after session init -- a poke before the race loads would stick, after init it does nothing per-frame but the baked value is the one used. See docs/42-ai-realism-and-difficulty-model.md.
